purpose: Define the exact, compilable v0.1.0 content of monokl's crate manifest (Cargo.toml's [package]/[lib]/[[bin]]/[features]/[dependencies]/[dev-dependencies]/[[bench]]/[lints] sections) and module-declaration file (lib.rs), per docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md Sections 1-2 (lines 46-189), together with the workspace root Cargo.toml content those sections depend on to resolve at all (Section 28, lines 3021-3078) -- so the crate implementer scaffolding monokl for the first time, and every subsequent track whose module must be declared in lib.rs to be part of the compiled crate, never has to guess a dependency, a dependency's pinned version, a feature flag's dependency list, a module's cfg gate, or whether the crate manifest and its workspace root actually agree with each other. Cargo's own inheritance mechanism makes the two files inseparable: six of monokl's [package] fields and its [lints] entry are `.workspace = true` references that Cargo refuses to resolve without a root manifest supplying them, and every one of monokl's 26 distinct workspace-shared dependency crates (27 `{ workspace = true }` entries total, since serde_json appears in two dependency tables) needs a workspace-level version pin to mean anything concrete -- locking Section 1 without Section 28 would describe a manifest whose `.workspace = true` references cannot resolve. This spec locks both together from the two documents that define them, states the concrete, mechanically-verified consequences of that locked content (build failures, publish restrictions, compiler warnings, workspace-inheritance failures), states a further, confirmed gap in what even those two documents together can resolve (the orin-cargo registry's own configuration is not part of this spec's corpus at all -- see AC-008B), and separately flags -- without resolving -- a discrepancy in a third, later document that could otherwise be mistaken for describing this same v0.1.0 baseline.
scope: Cargo.toml's [package] section (11 content lines: name, version, 6 workspace-inherited fields via `.workspace = true`, keywords, description, publish), [lib] section, [[bin]] section, [features] table (default, lang-ts, cli, miette -- each flag's exact dependency-activation list), [dependencies] table (io-errors path dependency plus 14 always-compiled core crates, 5 optional lang-ts-gated oxc_* crates, 2 optional cli-gated crates), [dev-dependencies] table (6 crates), [[bench]] entry, and [lints] entry -- all verbatim per 01-core-architecture.md:49-134 (Section 1's Cargo.toml code block). lib.rs's crate-level `#![cfg_attr(test, ...)]` attribute and its 15 module declarations (14 `pub mod`, 1 `#[cfg(test)] mod`) with their exact #[cfg(feature = ...)] gates, verbatim per 01-core-architecture.md:157-186 (Section 2's code block), cross-checked against the module-gating summary sentence at line 188. The workspace root Cargo.toml content Section 1 depends on to resolve: [workspace.lints.clippy] and [workspace.lints.rust] (the target of monokl's own `[lints] workspace = true`), [profile.release], [workspace.package] (the target of monokl's six `.workspace = true` package fields, with an explicit note on which of monokl's own [package] fields are NOT inherited from it -- and with 2 of workspace.package's 9 fields, rust-version and license, locked to values that intentionally diverge from Section 28's literal text, "1.85" and "MIT" respectively, grounded instead in the repository's actual LICENSE file and in michi's own Cargo.toml per AC-020), the workspace's resolver/members declaration, and the concrete version pin for every one of monokl's 26 distinct workspace-shared dependency crates (27 `{ workspace = true }` entries total) -- all verbatim per 01-core-architecture.md:3021-3078 (Section 28), except workspace.package's rust-version and license fields, which AC-020 locks to corrected values per the grounds above. It also locks the cross-file consistency fact that every feature name lib.rs's #[cfg(feature = ...)] gates reference (cli, lang-ts) is a key that actually exists in Cargo.toml's [features] table, and states the concrete Cargo/rustc-level consequences of several pieces of locked content: the required-features build behavior under explicit vs. implicit target selection (AC-003B), the publish-registry restriction (AC-001B), the unexpected_cfgs warning that would result if the cross-file feature-name agreement didn't hold (AC-015), and the workspace-inheritance failure that results if Section 1's manifest exists without Section 28's root (AC-025). Finally, it states -- as an explicit, non-resolving cross-reference -- that docs/spec/03-multi-language-platform.md's later 'new dependencies relative to Phase 1' list claims some dependencies as new that Section 1's own Cargo.toml already declares, and the differing concrete consequences of following that claim literally depending on which dependency table is involved (AC-016). It does not lock the moon.yml block's own content (see non_goals), or any content from Section 3 onward (error.rs, types.rs, etc. -- separate tracks, e.g. SPEC-001, SPEC-003).
non_goals: The moon.yml block's own content, shown immediately after Section 1's Cargo.toml (01-core-architecture.md:139-153) -- this track locks Cargo.toml and lib.rs, not moon.yml. Whether monokl's real scaffold should actually include a moon.yml is a project-tooling decision this track does not make: moon.yml is referenced elsewhere in this same source document as an expected project file (01-core-architecture.md:3168, listing `crates/monokl/{Cargo.toml,moon.yml}`), so this is not asserted to be stale residue -- only that its content is a separate concern from the two files this track locks. If the project ultimately decides against moon in favor of a different task runner, that is a design decision outside a manifest-content-lock track's scope.

The orin-cargo Cargo registry's actual configuration (a `.cargo/config.toml` `[registries.orin-cargo]` entry supplying its index URL, and any associated authentication) -- confirmed absent from every file in docs/spec/*.md (corpus-wide grep for 'registries.orin-cargo'/'.cargo/config' returns no hits). acceptance_criteria.criterion: Cargo.toml's [package] section (01-core-architecture.md:50-60, the 11 content lines following the [package] header at line 49) is exactly: name = "monokl"; version = "0.1.0"; six fields written with `.workspace = true` syntax (not literal values) in this order -- edition.workspace, rust-version.workspace, license.workspace, repository.workspace, authors.workspace, categories.workspace; keywords = ["monokl", "search", "ast", "semantic", "typescript"] (exactly these 5 strings, in this order); description = "AST-aware semantic code search for TypeScript/JavaScript and Rust."; publish = ["orin-cargo"] (an array containing one registry-name string, not a boolean). Of these 11 lines, name/version/keywords/description/publish are monokl's own literal values, not inherited from the workspace -- see AC-020 for which fields the six `.workspace = true` lines resolve to and confirmation that workspace.package's own version/keywords/publish fields (which do exist, at different values) are not what these five literal lines draw from.

Running `cargo publish` against any registry other than orin-cargo (e.g. `cargo publish --registry crates-io`) fails with a deterministic Cargo error stating the package cannot be published and that the target registry is not listed in the package's package.publish value in Cargo.toml -- publish = ["orin-cargo"] (AC-001) is an explicit allow-list, not a default suggestion. With no --registry flag supplied, cargo finds orin-cargo as the sole allowed registry and selects it automatically rather than erroring on an ambiguous-registry basis -- but the command then fails regardless (a distinct, later error: the orin-cargo registry's index cannot be found) unless a `.cargo/config.toml` `[registries.orin-cargo]` entry supplying that registry's actual index location exists somewhere in the build environment. See AC-008B for why this precondition is unavoidable and outside this track's corpus.
Cargo.toml's [lib] section (01-core-architecture.md:62-64) is exactly: name = "monokl", path = "src/lib.rs".
Cargo.toml's [[bin]] section (01-core-architecture.md:66-69) is exactly: name = "monokl", path = "src/main.rs", required-features = ["cli"].

The monokl binary target's required-features = ["cli"] (AC-003) produces three different Cargo behaviors depending on how it's built with the cli feature disabled (e.g. under --no-default-features). Explicit binary target selection -- `cargo build --bin monokl`, `cargo run`, or `cargo install --bin monokl` -- fails with a deterministic error naming the missing required feature and suggesting how to enable it. Implicit/default target selection -- a plain `cargo build`, `cargo test`, or `cargo check` -- succeeds with exit code 0 and silently omits the bin target from the build, producing no binary and no diagnostic at all. Bare `cargo install` (no --bin flag) is a third, distinct case: it also succeeds with exit code 0 and installs nothing, but unlike plain `cargo build`/`cargo check`/`cargo test` it is not fully silent -- it emits a warning that none of the package's binaries are available for install using the selected features. Because default = ["lang-ts", "cli"] (AC-004), any of these commands run with default features enabled does build/install the bin target without any special invocation.

Cargo.toml's [features] table (01-core-architecture.md:71-87) declares exactly 4 feature keys: default, lang-ts, cli, miette. default = ["lang-ts", "cli"] (line 72) -- exactly these two flags, in this order, no others.

The lang-ts feature (01-core-architecture.md:75-81) activates exactly these 5 optional dependencies, via dep: syntax, in this order: "dep:oxc_parser", "dep:oxc_ast", "dep:oxc_span", "dep:oxc_allocator", "dep:oxc_resolver". No other feature activates any of these 5 crates.

The cli feature (01-core-architecture.md:84) is exactly cli = ["dep:clap", "miette"] -- its second element is the bare feature name "miette" (transitively enabling the miette feature below), not the dependency-activation string "dep:miette". clap is enabled only via this feature; miette (the dependency) is enabled only transitively, through the miette feature this activates. This same source line is also cited as supporting fact inside SPEC-001.json's AC-002; a future revision to line 84 should re-verify both specs' criteria for consistency.

The miette feature (01-core-architecture.md:87) is exactly miette = ["dep:miette", "io-errors/miette"] -- it activates the miette crate itself (dep:miette) and forwards activation to io-errors's own "miette" feature (io-errors/miette). This same source line is also cited as supporting fact inside SPEC-001.json's AC-002; a future revision to line 87 should re-verify both specs' criteria for consistency.

Cargo.toml's [dependencies] table (01-core-architecture.md:90-118) declares io-errors as a path dependency with exactly these four keys: path = "../io-errors", version = "0.1", registry = "orin-cargo", default-features = false -- and no explicit features = [...] list.

AC-008's io-errors dependency, and any `cargo publish` of monokl itself (AC-001B), both reference the registry key "orin-cargo". Neither Section 1 nor Section 28 -- nor any other document in this spec's docs/spec/*.md corpus -- supplies the corresponding `.cargo/config.toml` `[registries.orin-cargo]` entry (the registry's actual index URL) that Cargo needs to resolve that key to a real registry. Without such an entry present somewhere in the build environment, resolving this manifest fails at parse/metadata time with a deterministic error stating the orin-cargo registry index was not found in any configuration -- this is true even with Section 1 and Section 28 both present and correct, since workspace-inheritance (AC-025) and registry configuration are two independent Cargo mechanisms. This track therefore does not claim, and AC-025 should not be read as claiming, that Section 1 plus Section 28 alone make this manifest independently resolvable end to end -- a third piece of environment configuration, outside this spec's corpus, is also required. See non_goals.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Stating a real, confirmed gap in what this spec's own corpus can resolve -- rather than silently letting AC-025's 'these two sections are what make the manifest parse' framing overclaim -- is a scope-honesty decision, not a fact this track can settle: the actual [registries.orin-cargo] entry's content (its index URL, auth mechanism) is genuinely not documented anywhere in docs/spec/*.md (confirmed via corpus-wide grep), so this track cannot lock it, only name that it's missing.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Cargo.toml's [dependencies] table lists exactly these 14 always-compiled (non-optional) core crates, each written as `{ workspace = true }` with no optional flag: blake3, camino, dashmap, grep-regex, grep-searcher, ignore, rayon, regex, rustc-hash, serde, serde_json, thiserror, tiktoken-rs, tracing (01-core-architecture.md:93-106). Combined with io-errors (AC-008), the crate has 15 dependencies that are always compiled regardless of which features are enabled. See AC-022/AC-023 for each crate's concrete version pin.

Cargo.toml's [dependencies] table lists the same 5 crates named by the lang-ts feature (AC-005) -- oxc_parser, oxc_ast, oxc_span, oxc_allocator, oxc_resolver -- each written as `{ workspace = true, optional = true }` (01-core-architecture.md:109-114). The 5-line block carries two textually and positionally distinct comments: a block-level header immediately before oxc_parser (line 108, "# lang-ts feature-gated OXC deps."), scoped to all 5 dependencies, and a second, dependency-specific comment immediately before oxc_resolver only (line 113, "# Versioned independently from OXC 0.128 suite — own 11.x line."), which does not apply to the other 4. AC-023 confirms this at the version-pin level: oxc_resolver's workspace version pin is "11" while the other four oxc_* crates all pin to "0.128".
Cargo.toml's [dependencies] table lists clap and miette, in that order, each written as `{ workspace = true, optional = true }` (01-core-architecture.md:117-118).

Cargo.toml's [dev-dependencies] table (01-core-architecture.md:121-127) lists exactly these 6 crates, in this order, each `{ workspace = true }`: insta, pretty_assertions, proptest, serde_json, tempfile, criterion. serde_json therefore appears in both [dependencies] (AC-009) and [dev-dependencies] -- both entries are real and both are `{ workspace = true }`, not a duplication error. This same [dependencies]/[dev-dependencies] coexistence pattern is the basis of AC-016's distinction between dashmap/rustc-hash (already in [dependencies]) and tempfile (only in [dev-dependencies]).

Cargo.toml declares exactly one [[bench]] entry (01-core-architecture.md:129-131): name = "pipeline", harness = false. It declares exactly one [lints] entry (01-core-architecture.md:133-134): workspace = true, inheriting the workspace's lint configuration (AC-017/AC-018) rather than declaring any lint level locally.

lib.rs (01-core-architecture.md:157-186) opens with the crate-level attribute #![cfg_attr(test, allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic))] (line 162, preceded by an explanatory comment at lines 158-161). It then declares exactly 15 modules, in this order, with these exact gates: pub mod analysis; (164, ungated) -- pub mod budget; (165, ungated) -- #[cfg(feature = "cli")] pub mod cli; (166-167) -- pub mod dedup; (168, ungated) -- #[cfg(feature = "lang-ts")] pub mod enrich; (169-170) -- pub mod error; (171, ungated) -- #[cfg(feature = "lang-ts")] pub mod indices; (172-173) -- #[cfg(feature = "cli")] pub mod output; (174-175) -- #[cfg(feature = "lang-ts")] pub mod pipeline; (176-177) -- pub mod query; (178, ungated) -- pub mod rank; (179, ungated) -- pub mod text_search; (180, ungated) -- pub mod tokens; (181, ungated) -- pub mod types; (182, ungated) -- #[cfg(test)] mod tests_types; (184-185, the sole non-pub module). 14 of the 15 are `pub mod`; only tests_types is a bare (non-pub) `mod`.

Of lib.rs's 15 module declarations, exactly 3 are gated #[cfg(feature = "lang-ts")] (enrich, indices, pipeline) and exactly 2 are gated #[cfg(feature = "cli")] (cli, output) -- matching verbatim the summary sentence at 01-core-architecture.md:188. The remaining 9 pub mod declarations carry no feature cfg and are always compiled; tests_types is gated on #[cfg(test)], a build-profile cfg, not a feature flag. Both feature names these gates reference are keys that actually exist in Cargo.toml's [features] table (AC-004). If either were absent, every #[cfg(feature = "...")] gate referencing it would trigger rustc's unexpected_cfgs lint, which is warn-by-default and only escalates to a hard build failure if promoted by the workspace root lint table (AC-017/AC-018) -- which, per AC-017, does not list unexpected_cfgs among its explicit entries, so this scenario would produce only a warning under the locked lint configuration, not a deny-level failure.

docs/spec/03-multi-language-platform.md's 'New runtime dependencies introduced relative to Phase 1' list (03-multi-language-platform.md:78-86) names dashmap, rustc-hash, and tempfile among dependencies it describes as newly introduced -- but Section 1's own v0.1.0 Cargo.toml, locked by this track, already declares all three: dashmap and rustc-hash in [dependencies] (01-core-architecture.md:95, :101, AC-009), and tempfile in [dev-dependencies] only (01-core-architecture.md:126, AC-012). Following that list literally has two different consequences depending on the crate: for dashmap and rustc-hash, both already declared in [dependencies], adding a second entry for either in the same table is a duplicate TOML key and the manifest fails to parse. For tempfile, already declared only in [dev-dependencies], adding a new entry to [dependencies] is a different table -- not a duplicate key -- so the manifest parses and builds successfully; the practical effect is a silent semantic change, promoting a dev-only dependency to a runtime one with no error or warning, the same [dependencies]/[dev-dependencies]-coexistence mechanism AC-012 already establishes for serde_json. This track does not resolve the discrepancy or correct 03-multi-language-platform.md's text; it states the discrepancy and its differing concrete consequences per dependency so a reader of that later document's list does not mistake its 'new' claim, or its implied uniform consequence, for this track's own ground truth. fs2, gix, ra_ap_syntax, and owo-colors, the list's other four entries, are not addressed by this criterion since none of the four appears anywhere in Section 1's Cargo.toml.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: Stating a downstream document's factual conflict with this track's own locked source, and the differing concrete consequences of following it literally, without attempting to adjudicate or correct that document, is a scope decision rather than a transcription fact -- per REQ-004's done_when item 3 and non_goals. This is the same 'flag, don't resolve' pattern already gated in SPEC-001's AC-015 (elided Git operation-tag sites) and SPEC-003's AC-007/AC-008 (naming contradictions with a concrete consequence). The dashmap/rustc-hash-vs-tempfile distinction matters because the two crates' consequences genuinely differ (duplicate-key parse failure vs. legal cross-table promotion, AC-012) -- a single uniform claim would misdescribe one of the two cases.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The workspace root Cargo.toml's [workspace.lints.clippy] table (01-core-architecture.md:3024-3039) declares exactly 15 entries: pedantic = { level = "warn", priority = -1 }; unwrap_used = "deny"; expect_used = "deny"; panic = "deny"; unreachable = "deny"; unimplemented = "deny"; dbg_macro = "deny"; todo = "deny"; print_stdout = "warn"; print_stderr = "warn"; await_holding_lock = "deny"; module_name_repetitions = "allow"; must_use_candidate = "allow"; missing_errors_doc = "allow"; missing_panics_doc = "allow". A source note immediately below this table (01-core-architecture.md:3050, "Post-research addition") states unreachable and unimplemented were added to the deny list after the original list denied panic but not these two, which let a real unreachable!("handled above") panic path in git_scope.rs's scope_files_with_index (since fixed to not need it) slip past the policy. This is the workspace-level lint configuration monokl's own [lints] workspace = true (AC-013) inherits in full; unexpected_cfgs is not among these 15 explicit entries (AC-015).
The workspace root Cargo.toml's [workspace.lints.rust] table (01-core-architecture.md:3041-3042) declares exactly one entry: unsafe_code = "deny".

The workspace root Cargo.toml's [profile.release] table (01-core-architecture.md:3044-3047) declares exactly three entries: lto = true, codegen-units = 1, strip = true. This applies to any `cargo build --release` (or equivalent release-profile build) anywhere in the workspace, including monokl, independent of the [workspace.lints.*]/[workspace.package] inheritance mechanism AC-017/AC-018/AC-020 describe -- profile settings apply by build profile, not by explicit per-crate opt-in.

The workspace root Cargo.toml's [workspace.package] table declares exactly 9 fields: version = "0.0.0"; edition = "2024"; rust-version = "1.96"; license = "AGPL-3.0-or-later"; repository = "https://github.com/orin-dx/monokl"; authors = ["Orin DX Contributors"]; keywords = ["orin-dx", "developer-tools"]; categories = ["development-tools"]; publish = false. Seven of these 9 fields (version, edition, repository, authors, keywords, categories, publish) are locked verbatim per 01-core-architecture.md:3055-3065 (Section 28) and are unaffected by this correction. The remaining two -- rust-version and license -- diverge intentionally from Section 28's literal text, which states rust-version = "1.85" and license = "MIT"; this spec locks the corrected values instead, per the two independent grounds stated in linked_research: (a) license = "AGPL-3.0-or-later" is grounded in the repository root's actual LICENSE file, which is AGPL-3.0 text, not MIT -- Section 28's "MIT" was an internal inconsistency in the source document, and the user has confirmed AGPL-3.0 is the correct license for this project; (b) rust-version = "1.96" is grounded in michi's own Cargo.toml (rust-version = "1.96"), since monokl depends on michi (github.com/orin-dx/michi) for agent-facing output rendering -- declaring rust-version = "1.85" while depending on a crate whose own MSRV is 1.96 would make monokl's MSRV declaration false. Of these 9 fields, monokl's own [package] section (AC-001) inherits exactly 6 via `.workspace = true`: edition (resolves to "2024"), rust-version (resolves to "1.96"), license (resolves to "AGPL-3.0-or-later"), repository (resolves to the URL above), authors (resolves to ["Orin DX Contributors"]), and categories (resolves to ["development-tools"]) -- matching AC-001's count exactly. The remaining 3 workspace.package fields -- version, keywords, publish -- are NOT inherited by monokl: monokl's [package] declares its own literal version = "0.1.0" (not the workspace default "0.0.0"), its own literal keywords (5 monokl-specific strings, not ["orin-dx", "developer-tools"]), and its own literal publish = ["orin-cargo"] (not the workspace default false). A workspace.package field existing does not by itself mean a given crate inherits it; only a crate's own `.workspace = true` on that specific field triggers inheritance, and monokl's Cargo.toml (AC-001) does not write `.workspace = true` for version, keywords, or publish.

The workspace root Cargo.toml declares resolver = "3" and members = ["crates/*"] (01-core-architecture.md:3067) -- a glob covering every crate directory under crates/, which includes monokl's own crate directory once scaffolded there.

The workspace root Cargo.toml's dependency version pins (01-core-architecture.md:3071-3074, the first four of eight bullet lines under "Relevant workspace dependencies for monokl") declare exactly these versions: thiserror = "2"; serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }; serde_json = { version = "1", features = ["preserve_order"] }; camino = { version = "1", features = ["serde1"] }; rustc-hash = "2"; ignore = "0.4"; oxc_parser = "0.128"; oxc_ast = "0.128"; oxc_span = "0.128"; oxc_allocator = "0.128"; oxc_resolver = "11"; rayon = "1"; regex = "1"; blake3 = "1"; dashmap = "5"; tiktoken-rs = "0.6". This is what every `{ workspace = true }` entry for these 16 crates (spanning AC-009 and AC-010) concretely resolves to.

The workspace root Cargo.toml's remaining dependency version pins (01-core-architecture.md:3075-3078, the last four of eight bullet lines) declare exactly these versions: grep-regex = "0.1"; grep-searcher = "0.1"; clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive", "env"] }; miette = { version = "7", features = ["fancy"] }; tracing = "0.1"; insta = { version = "1.47", features = ["yaml", "json"] }; pretty_assertions = "1"; proptest = "1"; tempfile = "3"; criterion = { version = "0.7", features = ["html_reports"] }. This is what every `{ workspace = true }` entry for these 10 crates (spanning AC-009, AC-011, and AC-012) concretely resolves to. Combined with AC-022's 16 crates, this track locks version pins for 26 distinct crates spanning 27 `{ workspace = true }` entries across [dependencies] and [dev-dependencies] (serde_json appears in both tables, per AC-012, contributing 2 entries for 1 crate) -- every one of the 26 crates has a corresponding version pin in Section 28, and Section 28 names no crate this track does not already list -- a full two-way match, independently re-derivable by counting both sides.

io-errors (AC-008) has no entry among Section 28's 26 workspace dependency version pins (AC-022, AC-023) -- it is not a `{ workspace = true }` dependency and is not expected to appear there. io-errors is declared as a direct path dependency with its own explicit version = "0.1" (AC-008), resolved via path = "../io-errors" rather than the workspace's shared dependency-version mechanism; the two version-pinning approaches (workspace-shared vs. direct-path) coexist in the same [dependencies] table without conflict.

A Cargo.toml containing AC-001's `.workspace = true` package fields or AC-013's `[lints] workspace = true` entry, placed in a crate directory with no reachable workspace root manifest, fails to resolve: Cargo reports a deterministic error stating it could not find the given field (e.g. edition, or lints) inheriting from the workspace root manifest's corresponding workspace-level table, and the crate does not build. This is why this track locks both Section 1 (the crate manifest) and Section 28 (the workspace root manifest) together rather than treating either as independently sufficient for workspace inheritance specifically -- Section 1 alone, without Section 28's [workspace.package] and [workspace.lints.*] tables, describes a manifest that cannot resolve its `.workspace = true` references. This does not mean Section 1 plus Section 28 together are sufficient to make the manifest resolve end to end in every respect: see AC-008B for a separate, independent precondition (registry configuration) that is also required and is not part of this spec's corpus.

Fifth correction pass. AC-020 corrected two of its nine [workspace.package] field values: license changed from "MIT" to "AGPL-3.0-or-later", and rust-version changed from "1.85" to "1.96". Both were disproven by the same contradiction report, for two independent reasons. (1) License: the repository root's actual LICENSE file is AGPL-3.0 text, not MIT -- Section 28's own "MIT" literal was a pre-existing internal inconsistency in the source document, unrelated to any design decision, and the user has explicitly confirmed AGPL-3.0-or-later is the correct license for this project. (2) rust-version: monokl is adopting michi (github.com/orin-dx/michi) as a dependency for agent-facing output rendering, per explicit user confirmation; michi's own Cargo.toml declares rust-version = "1.96", so monokl's prior rust-version = "1.85" declaration would be false the moment that dependency is added -- a real crate cannot declare an MSRV lower than a dependency it actually depends on. Both corrections were verified directly against real files (LICENSE, michi's Cargo.toml) rather than the source document, since the source document's own literal values for these two fields are exactly what's being corrected -- this is a deliberate, stated divergence from Section 28's verbatim text, not an error in transcribing it, and linked_research now names the real files that ground the two corrected values instead of the source document line range for those two fields specifically. The other 7 [workspace.package] fields, and AC-020's inheritance-count explanation (still exactly 6 of 9 fields inherited via `.workspace = true`, matching AC-001), are unchanged. No other criterion in this spec references license or rust-version: AC-001 refers to these fields only via `.workspace = true` inheritance syntax, not their literal values, so it required no change. No other SPEC-NNN track in this project's corpus references license or rust-version either.

Fourth correction pass, after axiom-exit-gate (a second, independently-built verification pipeline) found real issues even after three clean canon-exit-gate rounds. It re-tested AC-001B's auto-selection claim on a live toolchain and found the command still fails afterward (exit 101, registry index not found) unless the orin-cargo registry is separately configured -- a precondition confirmed absent from every file in this spec's corpus. It also found a more consequential gap: AC-008's io-errors dependency locks `registry = "orin-cargo"`, and resolving that key requires the same missing registry configuration -- meaning Section 1 plus Section 28 together, contrary to AC-025's prior framing, do NOT make this manifest independently resolvable end to end; a third precondition outside this spec's corpus is also required. Fixed: AC-001B corrected to state the command still fails afterward; new AC-008B added stating the confirmed gap and its consequence explicitly; AC-025 reworded to scope its 'these two sections make it resolve' claim to workspace inheritance specifically, cross-referencing AC-008B rather than implying total sufficiency; a new non_goal added naming the registry configuration as out of corpus. Also fixed a leftover from the prior round: purpose/scope still said 'monokl's 26 `{ workspace = true }` dependency entries' after AC-022/AC-023 had already been corrected to distinguish 26 distinct crates from 27 total entries (serde_json counted twice) -- propagated the correct phrasing to purpose and scope.

Third correction pass. Round 3 (canon-exit-gate, retry 2, fail): re-testing every behavioral claim on a live toolchain rather than trusting the correction narrative, the gate found bare `cargo install` (no --bin flag) was wrongly filed in AC-003B's explicit-target-selection failure bucket -- it actually exits 0 with a warning, a third distinct behavior neither the fail nor the fully-silent bucket captured; fixed by splitting into three stated cases. Also found two count/arithmetic self-contradictions: AC-022 said 'these 15 crates' while enumerating 16 (and AC-023 already correctly said 'AC-022's 16 entries') -- fixed to 16, and AC-023's completeness claim reworded to distinguish 26 distinct crates from 27 total `{ workspace = true }` entries (serde_json counted twice, once per table). AC-020 said 'inherits exactly 4 ... plus authors and categories ... 6 total' -- an internal contradiction between its own stated count and its own enumeration; fixed to state 6 consistently. All three fixes were re-verified against source/tested behavior by the gate itself before being applied, not merely asserted.

Second correction pass. Round 1: canon-verifier found all 16 original criteria cleanly supported; canon-auditor found the draft's is_error_case:false-only posture left real Cargo/rustc/TOML consequences of locked content unstated -- fixed with AC-001B, AC-003B, an extended AC-016, an extended AC-015, a new non_goal (workspace root out of reach), a reworded AC-010, and a cross-link to SPEC-001. Round 2 (canon-exit-gate, retry 1, fail): independently testing the four new tooling claims on real cargo/rustc, the gate found AC-003B falsely denied cargo's real silent-skip behavior for implicit target selection (fixed by splitting explicit-vs-implicit target selection into two distinct claims), AC-016's duplicate-key consequence was false for tempfile specifically (it lives in [dev-dependencies], not [dependencies], so adding it to [dependencies] is legal, not a duplicate key -- fixed by stating the two crates' differing consequences separately, cross-referenced to AC-012's existing serde_json note), AC-001B misnamed a Cargo field (registry.publish -> package.publish, fixed), and -- the most consequential finding -- the non_goal claiming 'no [workspace] table appears anywhere in [the docs/spec/*.md corpus]' was false: Section 28 (01-core-architecture.md:3021-3078) is a full workspace root Cargo.toml, in the same document, supplying every field AC-001's six `.workspace = true` keys and AC-013's `[lints] workspace = true` entry need to resolve, plus the concrete version pin behind every one of this track's 26 `{ workspace = true }` dependency entries. Rather than keep excluding real, necessary, in-corpus content behind a false rationale, this track's scope was expanded to bring Section 28 into scope alongside Section 1 -- the two are genuinely inseparable, since Section 1's manifest cannot parse without Section 28's root, a fact now stated directly as AC-025. Nine new criteria (AC-017 through AC-025) lock Section 28's lint tables, release profile, workspace.package (with an explicit, previously-easy-to-miss clarification that workspace.package having a version/keywords/publish field does NOT mean monokl inherits them -- it doesn't, per AC-001's own already-correct observation that those three are literal, not `.workspace = true`), resolver/members, and both halves of the 26-crate version-pin list, plus a two-way completeness check (every locked `{ workspace = true }` entry has a version pin, and every version pin corresponds to an already-locked entry) and the workspace-inheritance-failure consequence tying Section 1 and Section 28 together. The moon.yml non_goal was also corrected: 01-core-architecture.md:3168 references moon.yml as an expected project file, refuting the original non_goal's implication that it's mere stray residue -- the non_goal now states only that this track doesn't lock moon.yml's content, without asserting a scaffold should or shouldn't include one, since that tooling decision belongs to project scaffolding, not a manifest-content-lock track.
